#故事情节描述#  生成Picture 1Picture 2Picture 3三张图中的女孩唱歌对口型的视频。参考视频是歌词字幕提示器，女孩需按照参考视频白色字体显示时间按着歌词对口型，白色字幕开始出现的时间就是女孩开始唱的时间，白色歌词依次从左到右结束，代表歌词从开始到结束。没有显示白色歌词则不开口。Picture 1 高潮部分起帧，女孩头部边唱变晃动，空中下起雨，女孩身子和脸部有雨珠的效果。手不停放下又起来。然后参考Picture 2，补充人物连贯动作，最后平静收场用Picture 3，注意背景有变化，特别是图3背景和图2有变化，需要用运镜来调整，背景的雨不要停。Picture1Picture 2,Picture3 需严格按顺序参考 ，切不要硬切画面，引起环境和人物不协调不自然的变化，画面之间变化需补充动作、运镜等变化说明，以确保画面顺滑。参考视频里的任何画面、字幕、运镜等都不要参考生成，只是用于对口型时间参考，这和规则有冲突，但这里有这条为准备！
口型需参考音频对上，音频和参考音频1完全一致，1:1复刻。需要和音频同步且严格读这些字，不要自己发挥读其他的字，节奏和参考音频的发音时间一致以确保口型和音频一致。另外根据图片设计动作和表情，包括闭眼有感情的唱等。

请注意图画最右边一张是视频的首帧截图，前面的才是参考图片Picture 1Picture 2Picture 3等等，视频的首帧截图的目的是便于模型分析，请仔细辨别，请根据多参模型提示词规则生成英文提示词。

## Context
你是一位精通 ComfyUI 和 minimax h3 ref2va 多参模型的多图以及视频音频参考生视频提示词工程师。你的任务是根据用户提供的【参考图描述】和##故事情节描述#，生成专用于 minimax h3  模式的详细的自然语言的英文提示词，不要解释，不要翻译，你要思考过程。另外注意，参考图描述中，最右边一张是视频的首帧截图，前面的才是参考图片，请注意，视频的首帧截图的目的是便于模型分析，请仔细辨别。
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the main character from <Picture 1>. Preserve the character's identity, facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and other defining visual characteristics.
<Subject 2> is the second character from <Picture 2>. Preserve the character's identity, facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and other defining visual characteristics.
<Video 1> is the main motion and scene reference. Use its character actions, body movements, gestures, facial-performance timing, interaction timing, camera angle, camera movement, framing, shot progression, background environment, visual effects, and overall temporal structure as the reference. If <Video 1> contains visual or camera effects, reproduce those effects at the same corresponding moments, including effects such as camera shake, zoom-in, zoom-out, rapid push-in or pull-back, slow motion, speed ramping, motion blur, flashes, glow, particles, smoke, fire, sparks, fireworks, explosions, dust, debris, rain, snow, fog, screen shake, impact effects, transformation effects, and transition effects. Match their original timing, duration, intensity, scale, position, direction, and interaction with the subjects and environment. Do not add any visual or camera effects that are not present in <Video 1>.
<Audio 1> is the dialogue and voice reference for the target video. Preserve the exact spoken dialogue, speaker order, natural conversational pacing, pauses, timing, and corresponding voice timbres of the speakers, while synchronizing the target characters' lip movements and performances to the dialogue.

summary:
[reference generation + video editing + audio reference] Replace the original characters in <Video 1> with <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> while preserving the reference video's actions, poses, facial-performance timing, interactions, camera movement, framing, shot timing, scene layout, background, and visual effects. If <Video 1> contains visual or camera effects, reproduce the same effects at the corresponding timing; do not introduce any effects that are not present in the reference video. Use <Picture 1> and <Picture 2> to define the target characters' appearance and identity. Use <Audio 1> as the dialogue, voice-timbre, pacing, and timing reference. The generated characters must lip-sync naturally to the spoken dialogue. The final video contains no subtitles, captions, logos, or watermarks.

<Subject 2> (appears throughout the target video): fully_preserved - preserve the identity, face, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, and defining visual characteristics from <Picture 2>.

If visual or camera effects are present, preserve their original timing, duration, intensity, scale, position, motion, and interaction; do not add unreferenced effects.
<Audio 1>: reference - preserve the exact dialogue content, speaker order, voice timbres, speaking rhythm, pauses, emotional delivery, and conversational timing without directly copying unwanted noise or unrelated audio artifacts.

detailed_description:
Create a [cinematic / photorealistic / anime / stylized] video using <Video 1> as the primary motion, performance, camera, scene, and timing reference.
Replace the original main character in <Video 1> with <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>. Replace the original second character with <Subject 2> from <Picture 2>. Preserve each target character's face, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, body proportions, and identity consistently throughout the entire video.
The target characters must reproduce <Video 1>'s body actions, pose changes, gestures, walking or dancing rhythm, head movement, facial-expression timing, interactions, and spatial relationships as closely as possible. Preserve the original camera angle, camera height, focal distance, framing, camera movement, push-in, pull-back, pan, tilt, tracking, handheld motion, and shot-transition timing.

Preserve <Video 1>'s original background, environment, lighting, scene composition, props, visual effects, and overall visual continuity unless explicitly requested otherwise.

If <Video 1> contains visual or camera effects, reproduce them only at their original corresponding moments. Examples include camera shake, handheld shake, zoom-in, zoom-out, rapid push-in, rapid pull-back, slow motion, speed ramping, motion blur, flashes, glow, particles, smoke, fire, sparks, fireworks, explosions, dust, debris, rain, snow, fog, impact effects, screen shake, transformation effects, compositing effects, and transition effects. Match each referenced effect's timing, duration, intensity, scale, position, direction, movement, and interaction with the characters, environment, and camera as closely as possible. If no such effect exists at a particular moment in <Video 1>, do not add one. Do not invent, enhance, exaggerate, or introduce any visual or camera effect that is absent from <Video 1>.

When a character speaks, synchronize the mouth movement, facial muscles, expression, head movement, breathing, and gestures naturally to <Audio 1>.
Use stable speaker IDs in the order the characters first speak.
<Subject 1> (S1) says: <d>[Language] [EXACT ORIGINAL DIALOGUE]</d>
<Subject 2> (S2) replies: <d>[Language] [EXACT ORIGINAL DIALOGUE]</d>
If <Subject 1> speaks again:
<Subject 1> (S1) says: <d>[Language] [EXACT ORIGINAL DIALOGUE]</d>
If <Subject 2> speaks again:
<Subject 2> (S2) says: <d>[Language] [EXACT ORIGINAL DIALOGUE]</d>
Replace [Language] with the actual spoken language, such as [Chinese], [English], [Japanese], [Korean], or [Spanish]. Preserve the dialogue exactly in its original language. Do not translate, rewrite, shorten, or paraphrase the spoken lines unless explicitly requested.
If a reference character holds, picks up, puts down, or interacts with an object during <Video 1>, follow the reference video's timing and continuity. Do not force an object from the reference picture to appear before the corresponding moment in <Video 1>. The target character should acquire, hold, release, or interact with the object only when the source-video action requires it.
Maintain strict temporal continuity from beginning to end. Do not introduce extra actions, extra cuts, extra characters, or unrequested camera movements.
Remove all subtitles, captions, burned-in text, logos, channel marks, and watermarks from the source-video appearance. Do not generate any new subtitles, captions, text overlays, logos, or watermarks.
No subtitles. No captions. No on-screen text. No logos. No watermarks.

overall_soundscape:
Use <Audio 1> as the reference for dialogue timing, speaker voices, voice timbre, pacing, pauses, breathing, and emotional delivery. Preserve or reconstruct relevant environmental ambience and physical sound effects that correspond naturally to the actions in <Video 1>, including [footsteps / clothing movement / object handling / room tone / wind / impacts / crowd ambience / other sounds].
Keep dialogue clearly intelligible and synchronized with the correct speaker. Do not add unrelated voices, narration, or extra spoken lines. If the requirement is to reproduce the audio 1:1, keep it identical to the reference audio, or directly use the input audio, then output the prompt using: `<Audio 1>: fully_copy - reuse <Audio 1> 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track.`
